translations.zh: 襄尋徙北屈，將圖關中，進屯杏城，遣其從兄輔國姚蘭略地鄜城，使其兄益及將軍王欽盧招集北地戎夏，歸附者五萬餘戶。
translations.literal: Xiang soon moved to Beiqu, intending to take Guanzhong; he advanced and camped at Xingcheng, sent his cousin Yao Lan, aide to the state, to seize territory around Fucheng, and ordered his elder brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu to gather Rong and Xia of Beidi—more than fifty thousand households submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang soon shifted to Beiqu to seize Guanzhong, camped at Xingcheng, sent his cousin Yao Lan, aide to the state, against Fucheng, and had his brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu rally Beidi tribes—more than fifty thousand households came over.

translations.zh: 苻生遣其將苻飛拒戰，蘭敗，為飛所執。
translations.literal: Fu Sheng sent his general Fu Fei to resist; Lan was defeated and seized by Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng sent Fu Fei to meet him; Lan lost and was captured.

translations.zh: 襄率眾西引，生又遣苻堅、鄧羌等要之。
translations.literal: Xiang led his host westward in retreat; Sheng again sent Fu Jian, Deng Qiang, and others to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang drew his troops west; Sheng sent Fu Jian, Deng Qiang, and others to cut him off.

translations.zh: 襄將戰，沙門智通固諫襄，宜厲兵收眾，更思後舉。
translations.literal: About to give battle, Xiang was urgently remonstrated with by the monk Zhitong, who urged him to drill troops, gather his forces, and reconsider a later campaign.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiang prepared to fight, the monk Zhitong pressed him to drill his men, regroup, and wait for a better moment.

translations.zh: 襄曰：「二雄不俱立，冀天不棄德以濟黎元，吾計決矣。」
translations.literal: Xiang said: "Two heroes cannot stand together; I hope Heaven will not abandon virtue and forsake the black-haired people—my decision is made."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Two heroes cannot stand together; I trust Heaven will not abandon virtue and leave the people unaided—my mind is made up."

translations.zh: 會羌師來逼，襄怒，遂長驅而進，戰于三原。
translations.literal: Just then the Qiang army pressed close; Xiang grew angry and charged straight ahead; they fought at Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang host closed in, Xiang flew into a rage, charged forward, and met them at Sanyuan.

translations.zh: 襄敗，為堅所殺，時年二十七，是歲晉升平元年也。
translations.literal: Xiang was defeated and killed by Jian; he was twenty-seven years old—it was the first year of Jin's Shengping reign.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was defeated and killed by Fu Jian at twenty-seven—in the first year of Jin's Shengping era.

translations.literal: Fu Sheng buried him with ducal ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng buried him with ducal honors.

translations.zh: 萇僭號，追諡魏武王，封襄孫延定為東城侯。
translations.literal: When Chang usurped the title, he posthumously enfeoffed Xiang as Wei Wuwang and made Xiang's grandson Yanding Marquis of Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang seized the throne, he posthumously titled Xiang Wei Wuwang and enfeoffed Xiang's grandson Yanding as marquis of Dongcheng.
